---
title: "Fit, check, and revise a model"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 144
)
library(suppose)
```

A model can predict poorly for a reason that matters scientifically. This
worked example follows a temperature-only model, inspects what it misses, and
adds cure duration. The measurements are synthetic, constructed to illustrate
an omitted predictor. They provide no evidence about a real coating.

## Attach outcomes and predictors

Each row below represents an invented independent preparation. Temperature and
duration have separate identities and units in the retained predictor table.

Run this setup once to create `record` and `predictors`. Expand it to inspect
or copy the complete construction and provenance declarations.

<details>
<summary>Build the synthetic example record</summary>

```{r data}
temperature <- rep(c(140, 150, 160, 150), length.out = 40)
duration <- rep(c(50, 50, 70, 70, 60), length.out = 40)
strength <- 54 +
  0.4 * (temperature - 150) +
  1.8 * (duration - 60) +
  rep(c(-1, 1, -2, 2, 0), length.out = 40)
ids <- paste0("preparation-", seq_along(strength))
rows <- data.frame(
  observation_id = ids,
  condition = as.character(temperature),
  outcome = strength,
  batch = ids,
  specimen = ids,
  observed_at = "unknown"
)
record <- suppose_example()
observations <- import_observations(
  rows,
  source = "synthetic:documentation",
  protocol = "Invented independent preparations",
  author = "Tutorial analyst",
  units = "MPa",
  role = "update",
  exposure = "explored"
)
record <- record_observations(
  record,
  observations,
  "Inspect the synthetic measurements"
)
predictors <- regression_predictors(
  record,
  record$observations[[1]]$id,
  data.frame(observation_id = ids, temperature, duration),
  units = c(temperature = "degC", duration = "minutes"),
  source = "synthetic:documentation-predictors",
  author = "Tutorial analyst"
)
record <- record_predictors(record, predictors)
```

</details>

```{r preview, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(temperature, duration, strength)[1:6, ],
  col.names = c("Temperature (°C)", "Duration (minutes)", "Strength (MPa)"),
  caption = "The first six synthetic measurements."
)
```

The API checks matched measurement IDs. It does not silently remove rows with
missing outcomes or predictors. The supported workflow requires 6–500
independent measurements and one or two numeric predictors.

## Review a baseline prior

This regression has normal measurement errors with unknown common variance and
a proper normal/inverse-gamma prior. It is a new specification; it does not
convert the earlier two-condition elicitation automatically.

```{r baseline}
baseline_prior <- regression_prior(
  record,
  predictors$id,
  "temperature",
  location = 54,
  intercept_sd = 10,
  effect_sd = 20,
  noise_sd = 3
)
```

The prior location is the expected outcome at the predictor reference value.
`effect_sd` is in outcome units per meaningful predictor change. Default reference
values use predictor midranges and half-ranges, without inspecting outcomes.
`noise_sd` is the square root of expected noise variance, not a known measurement SD.
Review the prior predictive intervals before fitting. The wide intervals below
express the illustrative uncertainty supplied for this example.

```{r prior-check, fig.alt="Prior predictive outcome intervals for a temperature regression, before fitting the synthetic outcomes."}
plot_regression(baseline_prior, view = "prior")
```

```{r fit-baseline}
baseline <- fit_regression(
  record,
  baseline_prior,
  independent = TRUE,
  reviewed = TRUE,
  seed = 42
)
```

```{r residuals, fig.alt="Residual patterns from a temperature-only model of synthetic strength data. Duration is an omitted predictor available for inspection.", fig.height=5.5}
plot_regression(baseline, view = "residuals")
```

The synthetic construction makes duration important. Retain that concern before
fitting a second model:

```{r baseline-review}
record <- record_regression(
  record,
  baseline,
  choice = "neither",
  author = "Tutorial analyst",
  reason = "The temperature-only model misses the constructed duration effect.",
  reviewed = TRUE
)
```

## Add duration and compare on the same rows

Predictor order defines the baseline and extension. Shared priors and transforms
remain the same across the two models.

```{r extended}
extended_prior <- regression_prior(
  record,
  predictors$id,
  c("temperature", "duration"),
  location = 54,
  intercept_sd = 10,
  effect_sd = 20,
  noise_sd = 3
)
extended <- fit_regression(
  record,
  extended_prior,
  independent = TRUE,
  reviewed = TRUE,
  seed = 42
)
extended$comparison[c("extended_minus_baseline", "paired_se")]
```

The comparison uses exact leave-one-out refits and reports a paired standard
error. A positive extended-minus-baseline log-score difference favors the
expanded model's held-out prediction. Model search after examining the data is
still exploratory.

```{r comparison, fig.alt="Pointwise leave-one-out predictive comparison of the temperature-only model and the model that also includes duration."}
plot_regression(extended, view = "comparison")
```

Review joint predictive checks and residuals as well as the score. Simulation
intervals help distinguish a borderline check from a clear mismatch; a favorable
score cannot certify adequate fit.

```{r retain}
record <- record_regression(
  record,
  extended,
  choice = "extended",
  author = "Tutorial analyst",
  reason = "Duration addresses the constructed omission; this is an exploratory synthetic example.",
  reviewed = TRUE
)
```

Both reviews remain in the record. Use `predict_regression()` for new cases in
the original predictor units, or [plan the next measurement](research-design.html)
from a retained model. Interactions, hierarchical models, arbitrary formulas,
and regression-specific prospective commitments are not implemented.
